name: TRT clinics (online telehealth)

card.summary: Online and in-person clinics that prescribe testosterone replacement; mainstream medical sources cover TRT itself but little on telehealth providers.
card.aka: Online TRT providers, men's health clinics
card.note: TRT is a controlled prescription therapy with monitoring needs; clinic quality varies.

quick.overview:
TRT clinics are providers, increasingly online, that evaluate men for low testosterone and prescribe testosterone replacement therapy. Looksmaxxing communities discuss them as a way to access TRT.

Published reference sources describe TRT as a treatment for hypogonadism and note it is also prescribed for age-related decline, which they call controversial. They give little information specific to telehealth clinics.
quick.mechanism: The clinic model itself has no mechanism; the therapy it delivers is testosterone replacement, which supplements or replaces the body's own androgen [1].
quick.risks: Wikipedia lists possible risks of TRT including higher hematocrit, worsened sleep apnea, accelerated growth of existing prostate cancer, possible clot risk, and suppressed spermatogenesis, and says PSA and hematocrit should be monitored [1].

lead: TRT clinics are medical practices, many operating online, that assess men for low testosterone and prescribe testosterone replacement therapy (TRT). TRT supplements or replaces androgens and can be delivered by injection, gel, patch, pellet or other forms [1].

Wikipedia describes TRT as classic treatment for male hypogonadism and notes that prescribing it for age-related changes is controversial and under study. US use rose from 0.5% of men in 2002 to 3.2% in 2013, then fell to 1.7% in 2016 [1].

paras: No studies found on online TRT clinics as a category. Wikipedia reports that a 2024 Cochrane review found little clinically meaningful short-term erectile benefit of TRT over placebo, that hypogonadal men may see modest improvements in sexual function, mood and energy, and that the TRAVERSE trial found no increased cardiovascular risk versus placebo in men with hypogonadism [1].

The FDA investigated stroke and heart attack reports in 2014 and in 2015 said safety and benefit had not been established for low testosterone due to aging, requiring label warnings. In 2025, after TRAVERSE, it removed the black box warning while continuing to monitor risks such as blood pressure increases [1]. Nevada banned TRT for UFC fighters in 2014 [1].
Reported risks include raised hematocrit, worsened sleep apnea, effects on prostate cancer and fertility suppression [1].

timeline.event: FDA begins safety review of testosterone [1].
FDA requires label warnings, states benefits for age-related decline unestablished [1].
FDA removes boxed warning after TRAVERSE [1].
